definitions.explanation: Living to an old age; a long lifespan. Used for both people and things (such as long-running TV programs or products). Carries a positive connotation of a full, blessed life.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}の{長寿|ちょうじゅ}を{祝|いわ}う。
{日本|にほん}は{世界|せかい}でも{有数|ゆうすう}の{長寿|ちょうじゅ}{国|こく}だ。
examples.english: Japan is one of the world's leading countries for longevity.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}で{長寿|ちょうじゅ}な{人生|じんせい}を{送|おく}るために、{食事|しょくじ}と{運動|うんどう}のバランスが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: To live a long and healthy life, a balance of diet and exercise is important.

notes:
USAGE:
{長寿|ちょうじゅ} is a positive word associated with good health and blessings. It is commonly used in celebrations of elderly relatives reaching milestone ages.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長寿|ちょうじゅ}を{祝|いわ}う (to celebrate longevity)
- {長寿|ちょうじゅ}{社会|しゃかい} (aging society)
- {長寿|ちょうじゅ}の{秘訣|ひけつ} (the secret to longevity)
- {長寿|ちょうじゅ}{番組|ばんぐみ} (long-running program)
- {健康|けんこう}{長寿|ちょうじゅ} (healthy longevity)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese tradition celebrates specific ages as {長寿|ちょうじゅ} milestones: {還暦|かんれき} (60), {古希|こき} (70), {喜寿|きじゅ} (77), {傘寿|さんじゅ} (80), {米寿|べいじゅ} (88), {卒寿|そつじゅ} (90), and {百寿|ひゃくじゅ}/{百歳|ひゃくさい} (100). Each has traditional celebration customs.
